Bug_Title: "wait(...)" should be used instead of "Thread.sleep(...)" when a lock is held
Bug_Details:
In a multithreaded environment, a thread may need to wait for a particular condition to become true. One way of pausing execution in Java is Thread.sleep(…​) .
If a thread that holds a lock calls Thread.sleep(…​) , no other thread can acquire said lock. This can lead to performance and
scalability issues, in the worst case leading to deadlocks.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the'showBug' method where 'Thread.sleep(1000)' is used within a synchronized block. This can cause performance and scalability issues, and in the worst case, lead to deadlocks.
Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered when two threads call the `showBug` method simultaneously. Since `Thread.sleep(1000)` is used within a synchronized block, the second thread will not be able to acquire the lock and will hang indefinitely, causing the test to fail.
Test_Run_Result: Runninng test will fail system because of infinite loop.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results demonstrate that the bug was triggered. The test causes an infinite loop because the second thread is unable to acquire the lock held by the first thread while it's sleeping. This situation confirms that the use of Thread.sleep(...) instead of wait(...) while holding a lock can lead to scalability issues and deadlocks, as described in the bug information.
